newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador industry fears El Nino could hit cocoa.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador industry fears El Nino could hit cocoa.

text.p: Ecuadorean cocoa exports could suffer from heavy rains which have hit the country's main plantations, industry officials said.
"If this El Nino current phenomenum continues, producing heavy rains, then damage to the Christmas crop is expected," National Cocoa Exporters Association president Jose Carvajal told Reuters.
Continuing rain could cause fungus outbreaks, he said.
The El Nino pattern of warm ocean temperatures occurs every two to seven years with profound effects on global weather.
"If the rains keep up until August and September, then the end of year crop is going to be damaged," Carvajal said.
Ashley Delgado, one of Ecuador's largest cocoa exporters , shared Carvajal's concern.
"The main crop will be affected. We fear quality damage to the cocoa from September," he said.
Ecuador produces about 100,000 tonnes of cocoa beans a year, exporting 92 percent as beans or in processed form. Its main markets are the United States and the European Union.
One of the world's top 10 producers, Ecuador has 250,000 hectares of cocoa plantations.
